author: Cait Kelly
description:
The energy minister says Australia has 41 days’ worth on petrol in strategic reserve. Follow today’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Asked about Greens' concerns that the penalties for breaching the bill are $100 million for companies, which is not a lot for massive tech companies. Asked why the government won’t fine them a percentage of their global revenue like Europe does, she said:

I think the Greens and I agree on the fact that this is about changing the behaviour of big tech, and ultimately this is about the social licence, and no particular figure that we mandate in Australia is going to be enough for the world’s richest companies.

It’s got to be about what incentivises the change in behaviour
title: Australia news live: escalating Middle East conflict will see prices rise again, Chris Bowen says

author: Reuters
description:
OpenAI’s decision comes after dire warnings about rapidly progressing technology and lawmakers’ calls for new rules

OpenAI will not go public in 2026, Sam Altman said in a Fortune interview published on Saturday, citing safety concerns over artificial intelligence.

“I actually think that, given everything happening with safety, right now would be an ill-advised moment to go public, and we don’t feel pressure on that,” Altman, OpenAI’s CEO, told Fortune.

Continue reading...
title: OpenAI IPO will not happen in 2026 amid AI safety fears, Sam Altman says

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Molar from large mammal that once lived in North America is in ‘immaculate condition’ after discovery in Bay Area

A 10,000 year-old tooth in remarkable condition from an ancient Pacific mastodon, a large mammal that once inhabited North America, was recently discovered by a California scientist.

Brigid Lynch, a geomorphologist, was working at a preserve in San Mateo county, when she stumbled across a peculiar rock.

Continue reading...
title: Fossilized 10,000-year-old mastodon tooth found by California scientist

author: Henry Belot
description:
Exclusive: strategic rethink urges progressive activists to respectfully steer one-on-one conversations with One Nation supporters towards economic concerns

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The message from strategists was blunt: do not, however tempting, personally attack Pauline Hanson or call her a racist.

The request has been made to progressive campaigners and unionists who have been asked to start one-on-one conversations with One Nation supporters before the Victorian election in November.

Continue reading...
title: Do not call her a racist: anti-Pauline Hanson strategists tell campaigners character attacks won’t work in Victoria

author: Benita Kolovos
description:
Potholed roads are ‘devastating political advertising’ for the Victorian government – but Ben Carrol’s made them the focus of his campaign

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

At a press conference to celebrate the sold-out NFL match played at Melbourne’s MCG on Friday, the Victorian premier, Ben Carroll, was heckled on one issue.

“Fix the potholes,” a punter called out as they walked past the Victorian premier’s press conference.

Continue reading...
title: Labor has had 12 years to fix Victorian roads. Turning to ‘pothole populism’ now may be too late

author: Cait Kelly Inequality reporter
description:
Local council and state government attempting to move on residents living in an encampment by the river in Wagga Wagga

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

The New South Wales government paid for a homeless man in Wagga Wagga to be sent back to New Zealand instead of offering him temporary accommodation, in an attempt to move on residents living in an encampment by a river.

The local council and state government have been attempting to clear out the encampment for several months after a newborn baby died in May when its mother gave birth to twins in a tent.
title: NSW government paid for homeless man to be sent back to New Zealand instead of offering housing

author: Luca Ittimani
description:
Some buyers say they are ready to absorb the fallout of housing weakness if it means boosting home ownership across the board

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Falling property prices have come at the worst possible time for Alex Hogan and his partner. They are now weighing up whether they can afford to have another child.

Locked out of the established housing market, the Queensland couple resorted to buying a block of land to build a family home.

Continue reading...
title: ‘Small price to pay’: The young homeowners welcoming falling house prices even as it hurts them

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Trump, again trying to curate museum, says exhibit would stay until 2032 for 300th anniversary of Washington’s birth

Donald Trump asked the Smithsonian Institution to install a 30ft “Colossus statue” of George Washington outside the National Museum of American History, and a special exhibit honoring the nation’s first president, in a social media post late on Friday.

The president requested that the exhibit continue through February 2032, the 300th anniversary of Washington’s birth.

Continue reading...
title: Trump asks Smithsonian to install ‘Colossus statue’ of George Washington with exhibit

author: Keely Aouga
description:
Michael Diehl allegedly forged magistrates’ signatures in North Carolina to allow enough time for ICE to take custody of prisoners

A former Guilford county detention officer in North Carolina faces forgery charges in connection to 20 alleged forged Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainment documents, according to a Guilford county sheriff’s office (GCSO) news release.

Guilford county’s sheriff, Danny H Rogers, reported that on Friday the Guilford county magistrate’s office notified the GCSO of a potentially forged court document submitted by GCSO detention officer Michael Diehl, 40.

Continue reading...
title: Former US detention officer charged with 20 counts of felony forgery

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Lutnick said $500bn of estimated $1tn needed to fund checks to all US adults could come from new visa program

Donald Trump’s controversial proposal to give a $5,000 “dividend” to all US adults if Republicans maintain control of Congress in November’s elections would not be paid out from US tax revenues, according to the US commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick.

“It’s not tax money,” Lutnick said in an interview with NBC News, adding that the administration could “earn the money that Donald Trump wants to pay out, not from the deficit and not from taxpayers”.

Continue reading...
title: Taxes wouldn’t fund $5,000 Trump ‘dividend’ if Republicans win midterms, says commerce secretary

author: Joseph Gedeon in Washington
description:
Crowd member repeatedly said some Democrats ‘should be shot’ during Ted Cruz’s speech, without senator responding

On the night Republicans gathered to mourn the killing of Charlie Kirk and warn against the dangers of violent rhetoric, a crowd at the party’s irregular midterm convention in Dallas repeatedly called for a sitting Senate candidate to be shot, while the Republican senator at the podium never denounced or even noted the outbursts.

The outbursts came repeatedly during Ted Cruz’s Thursday night address at the American Airlines center, when he named a Democrat he accused of holding radical views. After the senator mentioned the New York City mayor, Zohran Mamdani, video footage depicts at least one audience member shouting: “He should be shot!” The same cry followed when Cruz named Michigan Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed, and again after he named Texas Senate candidate James Talarico. Cruz did not pause or respond to the shouting, and it remains unclear whether
title: Calls for Democrats to be shot go unchallenged at Republican convention

author: Alba Asenjo Domínguez
description:
Residents in Frederick, Maryland, shaken after clashes as activists decry violence from officers as ‘unconscionable’

Political leaders in Maryland are calling for investigations into the conduct of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officers as they clashed with protesters during a federal operation in a local community.

Residents of Frederick, a city about 50 miles north-west of Baltimore, are still shaken more than a week after ICE officers arrived in numerous vehicles and could be seen on video footage using batons on members of the public and driving their cars on to the sidewalk towards people.

Continue reading...
title: Calls for investigation after video shows ICE officers using batons on protesters

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
The Brookwood Church in Simpsonville only just disqualified Jerry Sidell from serving there in any capacity

A registered sex offender who was sentenced to prison in the 1980s after he told authorities that he had molested several boys whom he met through his religious work with Christian youth in Georgia was later allowed to participate for decades in ministry at a South Carolina church.

The Brookwood church, a southern Baptist institution in the South Carolina city of Simpsonville, only just disqualified Jerry Sidell from serving there in any capacity, after he joined it in 1999 and fulfilled various ministerial roles.

Continue reading...
title: Registered sex offender was allowed to participate at South Carolina church for decades

author: David Smith in Dallas
description:
President the star of the show at two-day convention, but party’s plan to treat November elections as referendum on Trump himself poses grave risks

“We’re going to have a good time listening to music,” Donald Trump told thousands of supporters in downtown Dallas before handing the mic to an opera singer, “because I’m getting a little bit tired of politics now.”

Millions of Americans seem tired of politics after a decade dominated by Trump. So the US president’s decision to close out this week’s first ever Republican midterm convention with a plea – treat November’s congressional elections as a referendum on Trump himself – was received by his Democratic opponents with glee.

Continue reading...
title: Trump personality cult alive and well in Dallas – will it power Republican midterm success?

author: Agence France-Presse
description:
Riyadh has increased its use of the East-West pipeline since the start of the Middle East war to bypass the closure of the strait of Hormuz

Saudi authorities said Friday drones launched from Iraq led to the temporary closure of a crucial oil export route used to bypass the lockdown of the strait of Hormuz.

Riyadh has increased its use of the East-West pipeline, which links Abqaiq, near the Gulf, to the port of Yanbu on the Red Sea, since the start of the Middle East war to bypass strait of Hormuz closed by Iran.

Continue reading...
title: Saudi Arabia shuts down oil pipeline, blaming drones from Iraq

author: Henry Belot
description:
NSW police say 18-year-old was operating drone when arrested and likely ‘conducting surveillance on someone or some premises’

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A Sydney teenager has been charged with murder after police accused him of operating a drone as part of a suspected botched gang hit in the city’s west.

Joshua Macdonald, 40, was shot dead at a Merrylands West home on 2 September in what police believe may have been a case of mistaken identity. He was not known to police and had no links to organised crime.
title: Alleged drone operator charged with murder after mistaken identity shooting in Sydney

author: Lisa Cox
description:
Former SBS newsreader had been accused by Zionist Federation of Australia of breaching Racial Discrimination Act when sharing X posts

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Federal court proceedings brought by the Zionist Federation of Australia (ZFA) against journalist Mary Kostakidis have been discontinued “by consent” with “no order as to costs”.

The former SBS newsreader had been accused by the federation of breaching the Racial Discrimination Act (RDA) by sharing two X posts about a speech by the late Hezbollah secretary general
title: Court case brought by Zionist federation against journalist Mary Kostakidis ended ‘by consent’

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
Prosecutors accused musician, born Durk Banks, of putting bounty on fellow rapper in retaliation for friend’s killing

Chicago rapper Lil Durk has been acquitted of all charges in a murder-for-hire scheme, in which a man was fatally gunned down in 2022.

Prosecutors had accused Lil Durk, born Durk Banks, of putting a bounty on Atlanta rapper Tayquian Bowman’s life in retaliation for the 2020 shooting death of Banks’s friend, fellow Chicago rap star King Von.

Continue reading...
title: US rapper Lil Durk found not guilty of murder-for-hire scheme

author: Henry Belot
description:
Officers found one 14-year-old’s ebike was capable of hitting 90km/h. Owners have two weeks to appeal the seizure before the bikes will be crushed

Dozens of high-powered and illegal ebikes have been seized by police on Sydney’s northern beaches just weeks after the force was granted new powers to destroy dangerous bikes.

The operation was part of a coordinated push with the NSW government to ensure people only ride legal ebikes that have not been modified to reach high speeds.

Continue reading...
title: NSW police seize 36 illegal ebikes on northern beaches that are now destined for the crusher

author: Uwa Ede-Osifo
description:
SF Gate reports bond for Vicky Kyung Mi Kim, 65, set at $10m after man found dead at couple’s Palm Desert home

A 65-year-old California woman has been arrested on suspicion of murder after allegedly fatally wounding her husband with a flagpole, according to SF Gate.

On 4 September, Palm Desert sheriff’s deputies responded to an “unknown trouble call” in The Enclave, a luxury condominium community. Upon arrival, officers located an individual with “traumatic injuries” that appeared to be from a physical assault and pronounced them dead.

Continue reading...
title: California woman charged with murder after allegedly killing husband with flagpole

author: Roque Planas and agencies
description:
Police have arrested Jacques Ratliff and ruled the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black woman, as a homocide

Police in Jackson, Mississippi, have arrested a man in the death of Tasia Fortune, a 29-year-old Black woman found hanging from a tree behind a vacant house last month. The state medical examiner on Thursday ruled Fortune’s death a homicide.

Jackson police chief RaShall Brackney-Wheelock said at a news conference Friday that police had secured search and arrest warrants for Jacques Ratliff and arrested him when they encountered him walking on the street.

Continue reading...
title: Man arrested over death of Mississippi woman found hanging from a tree
